newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia to follow US on funds - CBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia to follow US on funds - CBA.

text.p: A greater proportion of Australian funds would be directed into managed funds rather than into banks over time, following the expansion of mutual funds in the United States, Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) David Murray said on Tuesday.
There had been a massive explosion of the proportion of funds in pension or mutual funds in the United States, partly because funds in banks attracted federal deposit insurance, Murray said.
He said the pressure was not as great in Australia because there was no deposit insurance required for bank accounts, but any move here to deposit insurance would accelerate the trend.

"There is so much money now in the pension funds and in other units trusts that we are having a lot of funds looking for securities. We also have that capacity through securitisation to put them there and for those reasons I think we will see it accelerate," Murray said.
"The shift to managed funds is a very important shift for the regulators to understand and that is important for the Wallis enquiry to understand."

The government inquiry into financial regulation, headed by prominent businessman Stan Wallis, had raised the possibility of a compulsory deposit insurance, given that almost all bank accounts are not government guranteed.
Murray said he was campaigning to stop any attempt at a compulsory deposit insurance.
